Automobile Association testified in favor of the Airport Spur. Several elected officials and many private citizens testified against the Airport Spur because of the effects of noise and air pollution on Hamlin Garland School and the immediate neighborhood. A snokesman for the Milwaukee School Board again neither endorsed nor condemned the Airport Spur but was likewise concerned with the effects of air and noise pollution on Hamlin Garland School.
A summary of the entire testimony and the Division of Highway's responses at the March 25, 1969 and July 11, 1974 public hearings is contained in Sections IX and XI of this Final Environmental Impact Statement.
The people of Milwaukee County indicated continued public support for regional transportation planning in a county-wide advisory referendum held on Jovember 5, 1974. Voters endorsed completion of all segements of the proposed Milwaukee County freeway system, with the Airport Spur proposal receiving 50% for construction.
Vildlife.
The effect of urban wildlife is expected to be minimal since the route traverses the edges of residential development and crosses agricultural lands. Implementation of the project will eliminate some members of the small animal species that normally inhabit this type of area. Others will be merely displaced. Consultation with DNP has confirmed that no endangered species of plant or animal life will be disrupted by any of the alternative routes. Also see DNP's letter of comment page 211.
